name: Sydney
tagline: Harbour city of sails, surf and golden light.
whenBlurb: Warm and bright in the Australian spring (Oct–Dec) and autumn (Mar–Apr); Vivid lights up June, but the summer holidays are hot and busy.

ourTake.lede: Sydney is a harbour town before it is a city, so organise everything around the water, the ferries are the best value in Australian travel and the finest way to see the place. Do the Opera House and the bridge, then get out to the eastern beaches and the northern coves where locals actually spend their weekends. Skip Darling Harbour; give that time to a Manly ferry and a coastal walk instead.
ourTake.comeIf: You want harbour, beaches and a polished city with excellent Indian food, direct from Delhi.
ourTake.skipIf: You want a short-haul trip; Australia is far and deserves more than a few days.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Capella Sydney
credentials: World's 50 Best Hotels 2025 (No. 12), Best Hotel in Oceania
Forbes Travel Guide 4-Star (2025)
items.description: A restored Edwardian sandstone palace off Circular Quay, the finest hotel in the country, and it knows how to wear it lightly.

items.name: Park Hyatt Sydney
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide 4-Star (2025)
Travel+Leisure World's Best, perennial Sydney listee
items.description: On the harbour's edge between the Bridge and the Opera House, the most cinematic address in the city.

items.name: Crown Towers Sydney
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide 4-Star (2025)
Condé Nast Traveller Gold List, Barangaroo landmark
items.description: Sydney's tallest luxury tower, glass, light and altitude, with the harbour laid out far below.

items.name: Four Seasons Hotel Sydney
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide 4-Star (2025)
items.description: The surest hands on the harbour, a dress-circle view of the Opera House and service you never have to think about.

items.name: The Langham, Sydney
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide 4-Star (2025)
items.description: A quiet grande dame tucked into historic Millers Point, the calmest luxury in the city.

items.name: The Darling
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide 4-Star (2025)
The Darling Spa, Forbes Travel Guide 4-Star Spa (2025)
items.description: A polished, design-led tower above The Star, sleek rooms and one of Sydney's finest hotel spas.

credentials: Condé Nast Traveller, recognised Sydney harbour-view hotel
Home to Altitude, a landmark harbour-view dining room
items.description: High above The Rocks with the broadest harbour panorama of any city hotel, the Bridge and the Opera House in one sweep.

items.name: InterContinental Sydney
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide, recognised Sydney luxury hotel

credentials: Condé Nast Traveller Hot List, Sydney opening

items.description: A bold, design-forward tower over Darling Harbour, colour, energy and a spectacular rooftop pool.

items.name: Kimpton Margot Sydney
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller, recognised Sydney design hotel
A landmark Art Deco building of the CBD
items.description: A heritage Art Deco office block turned playful design hotel, one of the CBD's most characterful stays.

items.name: Pier One Sydney Harbour
credentials: A landmark heritage-wharf hotel of Sydney Harbour
Condé Nast Traveller, recognised harbour hotel
items.description: Built out over the water on a restored finger wharf, you sleep almost on the harbour, under the Bridge.

items.name: Ovolo Woolloomooloo
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller, recognised Sydney design hotel
A landmark heritage-wharf hotel of Woolloomooloo
items.description: A vast timber-and-steel heritage wharf turned bold design hotel, one of the most striking arrivals in the city.

items.name: The Old Clare Hotel
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller, recognised Sydney boutique hotel
A landmark design conversion of Chippendale
items.description: A former brewery and pub reborn as an industrial-chic hotel in the arty heart of Chippendale.

items.name: Establishment Hotel
credentials: A landmark hospitality address of the CBD
Condé Nast Traveller, recognised Sydney boutique hotel
items.description: A discreet, glamorous townhouse hotel above one of the city's great dining-and-drinking addresses.

items.name: Little National Hotel Sydney
credentials: A recognised contemporary Sydney design hotel
Condé Nast Traveller, noted value luxury
items.description: A clever, design-conscious business base with a soaring library lounge and a rooftop over the CBD.

items.name: Sydney Opera House
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: Jørn Utzon's sail-shells over the harbour are the reason the world pictures Sydney at all. Beyond the one-hour guided tour, an evening in the Concert Hall or a dinner at Bennelong turns the icon into an occasion the whole family remembers; ask for the backstage Access or private tour if you want it uncrowded.

items.name: Sydney Harbour BridgeClimb
items.description: You climb the steel arch of the 'Coathanger' to 134 metres above the water, harnessed and led in small groups, for a 360-degree sweep from the Heads to the Blue Mountains. Dawn and dusk climbs are the ones to book; there is a gentler Sampler climb for older or younger members of the party.

items.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge & Pylon Lookout
items.description: Even without climbing, the walk across the bridge's pedestrian path and the 200-step Pylon Lookout give you the classic Opera-House-and-harbour frame for a fraction of the effort. A calm, no-booking option for a multi-generational group that wants the view without the harness.

items.name: Circular Quay & a Manly Ferry Crossing
items.description: The 30-minute ferry from Circular Quay to Manly is the best-value harbour cruise in the world, Opera House, bridge, headlands and open sea, all for a transit fare. Sit on the top deck outdoors; grand-parents and children alike love it, and Manly's beach and Corso make a natural lunch stop.

items.name: The Rocks
items.description: Sydney's oldest quarter, where colonial sandstone lanes, the weekend market and harbourside pubs sit right under the bridge. Do a walking tour for the convict history, then let the family browse craft and food stalls; it is compact, atmospheric and easy on older legs.

items.name: Royal Botanic Garden Sydney
items.description: Thirty hectares of harbourside gardens wrapping around the Opera House, free to enter and blissfully green. The Aboriginal Heritage Tour and the calm lawns make it a gentle multi-generational morning; the Garden runs right into Mrs Macquarie's Chair.

items.name: Mrs Macquarie's Chair
items.description: A sandstone bench carved for a governor's wife in 1810, sitting on the point that gives you the single most famous view of Sydney, Opera House and Harbour Bridge together in one frame. Come at sunset; it is a five-minute stroll from the Botanic Garden.

items.name: Bondi to Coogee Coastal Walk
items.description: A 6km cliff-top path linking Bondi, Tamarama, Bronte, Clovelly and Coogee, arguably the most beautiful urban walk in Australia, with the Icebergs pool, sea, and (each October) the Sculpture by the Sea open-air gallery. Do a section rather than all of it with elders; the café stops at Bronte and Coogee are excellent.

items.name: Bondi Beach & Bondi Icebergs
items.description: The most famous crescent of sand in the country, with the photogenic Icebergs ocean pool cut into the rocks at its southern end. Lunch at Icebergs Dining Room with the pool and surf below is one of Sydney's set-piece meals, and the menu handles vegetarian requests with ease.

items.name: Bronte Beach
items.description: A smaller, family-favourite beach with a natural rock pool, grassy park and shaded picnic areas, calmer than Bondi and better for children and grand-parents. The café strip behind the sand does a relaxed breakfast before the coastal walk.

items.name: Taronga Zoo
items.description: A hillside zoo across the harbour with koalas, kangaroos and giraffes framed against the Opera House and city skyline, reached by a scenic ferry and cable car. Kids adore it; the Roar & Snore overnight and private keeper experiences are the premium way to do it.

items.name: Art Gallery of New South Wales & Sydney Modern (Naala Badu)
items.description: The state gallery pairs a grand 19th-century building with SANAA's Pritzker-winning Sydney Modern (Naala Badu), opened 2022, Australia's finest Aboriginal art holdings alongside major international shows. Free general entry, world-class, and a serene indoor option on a hot or rainy day.

items.name: Australian Museum
items.description: The country's oldest museum, strong on natural history, dinosaurs and a deep First Nations gallery, engaging across every age in the family. Well air-conditioned and central, it is a reliable half-day when the weather turns.

items.name: Barangaroo Reserve & the Barangaroo precinct
items.description: A reclaimed headland turned into a native-planted harbour park, backed by a glossy waterfront of restaurants and the Crown Sydney tower. Walk the foreshore at golden hour, then dine, this is where much of Sydney's newest fine dining and vegetarian-friendly kitchens have clustered.

items.name: Queen Victoria Building
items.description: A restored 1898 Romanesque arcade, stained glass, tiled floors and a copper dome, housing boutiques over three levels. A refined, cool-in-summer place to shop and take tea; the architecture alone earns the visit.

items.name: Sydney Tower Eye & Skywalk
items.description: The city's tallest structure, with a glass observation deck 250 metres up and an open-air Skywalk for the brave. The clearest single overview of how harbour, beaches and bushland fit together, good for orienting the family on day one.

items.name: Darling Harbour
items.description: A pedestrian waterfront of museums, aquarium and restaurants built for families, everything walkable around the water. The hub for SEA LIFE, WILD LIFE and the maritime museum, with plenty of casual dining that caters to vegetarians.

items.name: SEA LIFE Sydney Aquarium
items.description: Walk-through ocean tunnels with sharks, rays and one of the world's largest Great Barrier Reef displays, plus dugongs found in only a handful of aquariums worldwide. A dependable, weather-proof crowd-pleaser for younger children.

items.name: Australian National Maritime Museum
items.description: Floating exhibits including a destroyer, a submarine and a replica of Cook's Endeavour, alongside migration and Indigenous seafaring stories. Hands-on and open-air enough to keep restless kids happy between the galleries.

items.name: Watsons Bay & South Head
items.description: A harbourside village at the mouth of the harbour, with the dramatic ocean cliffs of The Gap on one side and calm Camp Cove on the other. Take the ferry out, walk to the Hornby Lighthouse, then eat seafood by the water, a classic, unhurried Sydney afternoon.

items.name: Paddington
items.description: Leafy Victorian terraces with iron-lace balconies, the Saturday Paddington Markets, and Oxford Street's boutiques and galleries. The most elegant neighbourhood wander in the city, and where much of Sydney's independent designer shopping lives.

items.name: Surry Hills
items.description: Sydney's dining heartland, narrow streets packed with acclaimed restaurants, specialty coffee and wine bars. The place to send serious eaters in the family, with strong vegetarian and modern-Australian options at every price point.

items.name: Chinatown & Spice Alley
items.description: Paddy's Markets, dumpling houses and the laneway hawker stalls of Spice Alley make this the city's best-value, most vibrant eating quarter. A lively, affordable night out with plenty of vegetarian pan-Asian choices.

items.name: Chinese Garden of Friendship
items.description: A walled classical Chinese garden of pavilions, koi ponds and waterfalls, built as a gift from Guangzhou, an oasis of calm beside busy Darling Harbour. The tea house and quiet paths suit elders who want to sit and slow down.

items.name: Hyde Park & St Mary's Cathedral
items.description: The city's oldest public park, with a grand fig-tree avenue and the Archibald Fountain, facing the sandstone Gothic St Mary's Cathedral. A green, central spot to regroup between museums and shopping.

items.name: The Grounds of Alexandria
items.description: A former industrial site turned garden café, bakery and market with an ornate, Instagram-famous flower-filled setting. A relaxed, veg-friendly brunch destination that delights children and photographers alike.

items.name: Cockatoo Island (Wareamah)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Australian Convict Sites
items.description: The harbour's largest island, a UNESCO-listed former convict prison and shipyard, reached by ferry, now a heritage site you can walk and even stay overnight on. A quirky, atmospheric half-day away from the crowds.

items.name: Manly & the Manly to Spit Bridge Walk
items.description: Beyond the famous ferry and surf beach, the 10km Spit-to-Manly track threads secluded coves, Aboriginal rock engravings and bush, one of the finest coastal walks near the city. Do the ferry-and-beach version with elders, the full walk with the active.

items.name: Palm Beach & Barrenjoey Lighthouse
items.description: The glamorous tip of the Northern Beaches, long golden sand, the 1881 Barrenjoey Lighthouse headland, and the setting of TV's 'Home and Away'. A gorgeous day trip; arrive by seaplane from Rose Bay for the ultimate discreet flourish.

items.name: Rose Bay Seaplane Scenic Flight
items.description: Australia's oldest seaplane base, where a private floatplane lifts off the water for a sweep over the harbour, beaches and coast, and can drop you at a waterfront lunch at Palm Beach or Cottage Point. A private-charter treat that turns a meal into a memory.

items.name: Blue Mountains (Three Sisters, Katoomba & Scenic World)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Greater Blue Mountains Area
items.description: A vast wilderness of eucalypt-blue valleys, the iconic Three Sisters rock formation, and Scenic World's steepest-in-the-world railway and cliff-hugging cable cars. An easy full-day escape; charter a private guide and finish with high tea at the Hydro Majestic hotel.

items.name: Hunter Valley Wine Country
items.description: Australia's oldest wine region, 150-plus cellar doors famed for Semillon and Shiraz, set among rolling vineyards with fine dining and hot-air balloons at dawn. A private car and a curated cellar-door route, with a vegetarian-friendly long lunch, make a superb full day or overnight.

items.name: Royal National Park
items.description: The world's second-oldest national park, clifftop coast walks, the Instagram-famous Figure 8 Pools, Wattamolla lagoon and empty beaches, all an hour from the city. A wilder, quieter day out for a family that wants nature over crowds.

items.name: Featherdale Wildlife Park
items.description: A hands-on wildlife park where you can hand-feed kangaroos and stand beside koalas, the easiest close-up with Australian animals near the city, and a natural stop on the way to the Blue Mountains. Children love it; keeper encounters can be arranged privately.

items.name: Vaucluse House & Nielsen Park
items.description: A grand colonial Gothic estate with harbour gardens, beside the sheltered netted beach and shady lawns of Nielsen Park (Shark Beach). A refined, low-key eastern-suburbs afternoon combining history, a swim and a garden tea.

items.name: Cockle Bay & King Street Wharf dining
items.description: A curved harbour promenade of waterfront restaurants and bars overlooking the city lights. An easy, walkable place for an evening meal with the family, with plenty of choice for vegetarians and fussy young palates.

items.name: Carriageworks Farmers Market
items.description: Saturday's best food market, restored rail workshops filled with the region's growers, bakers and producers, alongside a leading contemporary arts venue. A genuinely local morning for food-lovers, with excellent produce and coffee.

items.name: Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park & West Head
items.description: Rugged bushland dropping to the Hawkesbury, with ancient Aboriginal rock engravings and the sweeping West Head lookout over Pittwater and Palm Beach. Combine with a Palm Beach seaplane or boat day for a spectacular, uncrowded north-of-the-city outing.

items.name: Luna Park Sydney
items.description: A heritage-listed 1935 amusement park under its famous grinning-face entrance, right beneath the Harbour Bridge with knockout city views. Old-fashioned fun for children and a nostalgic photo stop for everyone else.

items.name: Wendy Whiteley's Secret Garden
items.description: A lush, artist-created garden built by hand on former railway land, tumbling down to the harbour on the north shore, free, hidden and quietly magical. A serene detour few tourists find, lovely with grand-parents in tow.

items.name: Government House & the Domain
items.description: The Governor's grand Gothic Revival residence, its rooms open on guided tours and its gardens open daily, set in the parkland above the harbour. A stately, uncrowded window onto Sydney's colonial grandeur.

items.name: Newtown & King Street
items.description: Sydney's bohemian spine, street art, vintage boutiques, live music and one of the city's densest, most vegetarian-friendly eat streets. A change of pace from the harbour for older kids and food-curious adults.

items.name: Sydney Fish Market
items.description: One of the largest fish markets in the Southern Hemisphere, with a working auction, seafood counters and waterfront eating. Go early; a lively, no-fuss stop, though a family will want to pair it with vegetarian options elsewhere.

items.name: Cabramatta
items.description: The most authentic Vietnamese and South-East Asian quarter in Australia, pho, herb-heavy noodle bowls and market stalls at everyday prices. A rewarding culinary excursion for adventurous eaters, with abundant vegetarian choice.

items.name: Bradleys Head & the Mosman foreshore
items.description: A wooded harbour headland with a coastal track, a naval mast memorial and postcard views straight back to the city skyline. A quiet, leafy walk that pairs naturally with a visit to nearby Taronga Zoo.

items.name: Chippendale & White Rabbit Gallery
items.description: A regenerated inner-city pocket around the green-walled One Central Park building, home to White Rabbit, one of the world's finest collections of contemporary Chinese art, free to enter. A sharp, uncrowded cultural stop with a good tea house.

items.name: Oncore by Clare Smyth
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Three Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Clare Smyth's Sydney room, the three-star London chef's ode to Australian produce, high over the harbour.

items.name: Quay
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Three Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Peter Gilmore's harbourside icon, the Opera House framed in the window and cooking to match the view.

items.name: Saint Peter
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Three Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Josh Niland's fin-to-tail seafood, the most original fish cooking in the world, in a handsome pub dining room.

items.name: Sixpenny
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Three Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: A tiny, produce-obsessed inner-west room that quietly cooks at the very top of the national game.

items.name: Aria
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: A grand harbour-edge dining room staring straight at the Opera House, polished, celebratory, unmistakably Sydney.

items.name: Bennelong
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Peter Gilmore's kitchen inside the sails of the Opera House itself, you dine within a World Heritage landmark.

items.name: Yoshii's Omakase
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: A serene sushi counter of great purity, one of Sydney's finest omakase seats.

items.name: a'Mare
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Alessandro Pavoni's coastal Italian at Crown, pasta and seafood of real refinement, harbour at the window.

items.name: Bentley Restaurant + Bar
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Brent Savage and Nick Hildebrandt's progressive, wine-led cooking, one of Sydney's most quietly ambitious kitchens.

items.name: Firedoor
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Lennox Hastie cooks over live fire and nothing else, the most primal, precise wood-fire room in the country.

items.name: Ester
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: A wood-fired inner-west favourite of honest, seasonal cooking, one of Sydney's most-loved rooms for a decade.

items.name: Icebergs Dining Room and Bar
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Italian cooking above the Bondi Icebergs pool, the most glamorous beach view in Sydney over a long lunch.

items.name: Rockpool Bar & Grill
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Grand Art Deco steakhouse glamour, dry-aged beef and a legendary wine list in a soaring 1930s banking hall.

items.name: Bathers' Pavilion
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Serene modern cooking in a Mediterranean-white pavilion right on Balmoral Beach, a lovely harbour-beach escape.

items.name: Margaret
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Neil Perry's warm, produce-first neighbourhood room, generous cooking in the city's smartest suburb.

items.name: Shell House Dining Room & Terrace
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: A glamorous heritage-tower dining room and terrace, one of the CBD's most beautiful rooms to eat in.

items.name: Spice Temple
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Neil Perry's dark, sultry basement of regional Chinese heat, the antidote to polite Cantonese.

items.name: Ormeggio at The Spit
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Alessandro Pavoni's refined Italian on the water at The Spit, pasta and a marina view in equal measure.

items.name: Porteno
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Argentine live-fire asado in a buzzing Surry Hills room, whole animals over the coals, and a party every night.

items.name: Yellow
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: A pioneering vegetable-led tasting menu in a former artists' haunt, plant cooking at its most inventive.

items.name: Aalia
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Modern Middle Eastern cooking with real finesse, one of the CBD's most exciting recent tables.

items.name: King Clarence
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Live-fire and live-tank seafood cooked on a custom barbecue, bold, contemporary and hard to book.

items.name: Pilu at Freshwater
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Sardinian cooking in a heritage beach house above Freshwater, a serene northern-beaches lunch.

items.name: Cafe Paci
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Pasi Petanen's idiosyncratic, personality-filled cooking, a critical darling of the inner west.

items.name: LuMi Dining
credentials: The Good Food Guide, Two Hats (2025/2026)
items.description: Italian-Japanese cooking on a Pyrmont wharf, delicate, precise and quietly one of the city's best.

items.name: Otto Ristorante
credentials: The Good Food Guide, One Hat (2025/2026)
items.description: The glamorous waterfront Italian that has anchored Woolloomooloo wharf for years, see-and-be-seen dining.

items.name: Catalina
credentials: The Good Food Guide, One Hat (2025/2026)
items.description: Seafood and sparkling water views at Rose Bay, the seaplanes taking off past your table.

items.name: Clam Bar
credentials: The Good Food Guide, One Hat (2025/2026)
items.description: A glamorous martini-and-seafood room from the Swillhouse team, the CBD's most stylish new classic.

items.name: Kiln
credentials: The Good Food Guide, One Hat (2025/2026)
items.description: A rooftop room of live-fire, Korean-inflected cooking above the Ace Hotel, sharp food and a skyline view.

items.name: Cho Cho San
credentials: The Good Food Guide, One Hat (2025/2026)
items.description: Stylish modern Japanese in the heart of Potts Point, sharp cooking in a beautiful pale-timber room.

items.name: Continental Deli
credentials: The Good Food Guide, One Hat (2025/2026)
items.description: A playful deli-bar of tinned fish, martinis on tap and clever bistro plates, Newtown at its most fun.

items.name: Poly
credentials: The Good Food Guide, One Hat (2025/2026)
items.description: The relaxed all-day sibling to Ester, modern plates and natural wine in a stripped-back Surry Hills room.

items.name: Bar Copains
credentials: The Good Food Guide, One Hat (2025/2026)
items.description: A tiny, wine-soaked French bistro-bar, a short, perfect menu and a cult following.

items.name: Abhi's Indian Restaurant
credentials: The Good Food Guide, One Hat (2025/2026)
items.description: A long-running, genuinely hatted Indian kitchen, refined regional cooking well beyond the curry-house norm.

items.name: Ho Jiak Town Hall
credentials: The Good Food Guide, One Hat (2025/2026)
items.description: Punchy, generous Malaysian street cooking taken to a hatted level, one of the city's most exciting Asian rooms.

items.name: Pellegrino 2000
credentials: The Good Food Guide, One Hat (2025/2026)
items.description: A moody, red-lit Italian-American diner-bar, pasta, negronis and Surry Hills swagger.

items.name: McRae Bar, Capella Sydney
credentials: Inside Capella Sydney, World's 50 Best Hotels 2025 (No. 12)
items.description: A Victorian-era drinking den reborn inside the country's finest hotel, intimate cocktails under sandstone and low light.

items.name: Maybe Sammy
credentials: World's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 42), the only Sydney bar on the list
World's 50 Best Bars, listed every year since 2019
items.description: Rat Pack glamour in a room of pastels and pink dinner jackets, Sydney's world-ranked cocktail bar, seven years running.

items.name: Cantina OK!
credentials: Australian Bar Awards 2025, Tequila Bar of the Year
World's 50 Best Bars, former listee
items.description: A standing-room-only agave den in a former garage, twenty drinkers, mezcal poured with real love, and a global reputation.

items.name: Bar Planet
credentials: Australian Bar Awards 2025, Gin Bar of the Year
items.description: A slick, spirit-nerd gin bar with one of the deepest botanical lists in the country.

items.name: Kittyhawk
credentials: A celebrated Sydney cocktail bar, from the team behind The Lobo
items.description: A handsome bar imagining liberation-day Paris, rum, rye and ten versions of the Old Fashioned.

items.name: Dean & Nancy on 22
credentials: Australian Bar Awards 2025, Hotel Bar of the Year
items.description: A soaring 22nd-floor hotel bar of Art Deco glamour and a whisky room, the finest hotel bar in the country.

items.name: Old Mate's Place
credentials: Australian Bar Awards 2025, Bar of the Year
items.description: A hidden rooftop-and-library bar over the CBD, plants, an open fire and a garden terrace, named the country's best.

items.name: Altitude Bar, Shangri-La Sydney
credentials: A landmark harbour-view bar of The Rocks
items.description: A high-floor harbour bar with the Bridge and the Opera House laid out beneath the glass, the broadest view in the city over a drink.

items.name: Ramblin' Rascal Tavern
credentials: Australian Bar Awards 2025, Best Bartenders' Bar
items.description: A cult basement tavern where the industry drinks, irreverent, expert and gloriously unpretentious.

plan.heading: 4 days in Sydney, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Check into Park Hyatt Sydney at the foot of the Bridge, with the Opera House across the water.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Botanic Garden and Mrs Macquarie's Point for the classic harbour view.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Quay overlooking Circular Quay, Peter Gilmore's signature tasting menu.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Bondi to Bronte coastal walk before the sun is high.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch at Icebergs above the Bondi sea pool, then time on the sand.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Bennelong inside the Opera House sails.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A private launch across the harbour to Manly and the quiet northern coves.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Art Gallery of New South Wales and its new Naala Badu wing.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Firedoor, Lennox Hastie's live-fire kitchen in Surry Hills.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Drive to the Blue Mountains for the Three Sisters and the eucalypt escarpment.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A long lunch and cellar visit, then an unhurried return.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A final harbour-side dinner at Aria at Circular Quay.

items.name: The Rocks / Circular Quay
items.description: Historic and central, on the harbour and the ferries; the obvious first-timer base.

items.name: Potts Point / Elizabeth Bay
items.description: Elegant, walkable and full of good tables; suits those who want charm near the centre.

items.name: Bondi
items.description: Beach-focused and social, a bus ride from town; for travellers who want sand over skyline.

events.name: Sydney New Year's Eve
events.note: The world's headline midnight fireworks, staged off the bridge and harbour.

events.name: Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras
events.note: Weeks of events building to the Oxford Street parade, one of the world's largest.

events.name: Vivid Sydney
events.note: The city lights up nightly with projections, music and ideas across the harbour.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Indian passport holders need an ETA or visitor visa arranged before travel; stay around Circular Quay or the eastern beaches, and a concierge can arrange a private yacht on the harbour and tables at Quay or Bennelong.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Land at Kingsford Smith (SYD), a 20 to 30-minute chauffeured run to the harbour; for a memorable entrance, a seaplane from Rose Bay can deliver you along the coast.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: The harbour city is best mixed: a private car for distance, walking the Rocks and Botanic Gardens, and the ferries, which are the loveliest way to see it from the water.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: eSIM (Telstra or Optus) gives excellent 5G everywhere; wifi is universal.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Currency is the Australian dollar; cards and phone payments are accepted everywhere and cash is rarely needed; tipping is modest and optional, around 10 percent for fine dining.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: Southern seasons flipped: Oct-Nov and Mar-Apr are warm, clear and uncrowded; Dec-Feb is hot, humid and peak-holiday, and Jun-Aug is cool and wetter though still mild.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Air India flies Delhi-Sydney nonstop on the 787, about 13.5h; from Mumbai or Bengaluru route via Singapore (Singapore Airlines) or Delhi. Qantas serves Bengaluru-Sydney but the route is suspended 8 Aug-24 Oct 2026, so confirm before booking. Fly Singapore Airlines business via Changi for the smoothest one-stop and use The Private Room / SilverKris lounge.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No mandatory vaccinations; Australia has strict biosecurity, so declare all food including anything veg/Jain you carry. Tap water is safe. Sydney is very safe with excellent private healthcare. Sun is intense, factor UV protection.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Excellent for vegetarians and Jain travellers; large Indian community means abundant, genuine Indian food and pure-veg kitchens, and most fine dining does serious vegetarian menus. Harris Park is the Indian food hub, and the city's vegetarian and vegan options are extensive.
